title: Goan Pork Vindaloo
subtitle: Original Version
headnote: This untested original version was written to approximate a mild, slightly sweet Central Market vindaloo. Review the spice-mixing directions, which include both a simple mixing instruction and a separate toasting and grinding method.

ingredientGroups.title: Vindaloo
items: 2½ lb pork butt, cut into chunks
¼ cup chopped cilantro, to garnish

ingredientGroups.title: Rice
items: ¼ cup daikon radish, small dice

steps: Mix the seasoned vinegar ingredients and set aside. The source also says to mix the spices and set aside, then offers the following toasting and grinding method.
Toast the spices over medium heat for 30–60 seconds, or on a sheet pan in a 250–275°F oven for 15 minutes. Cool for 5 minutes, then grind finely.

Rinse the rice and cook according to the rice cooker directions; the source gives a typical rice-to-water ratio of 1:1 to 1:1.25. Fold in the chickpeas, shallot, daikon, oil and lemon juice while the rice is warm.
Heat 3 Tbsp neutral oil in a Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Working in 3–4 batches, lightly brown the pork and set aside before a hard crust forms.
Reduce the heat to medium and sauté the onions for 6–8 minutes, until soft and lightly golden. Add a small pinch of salt, the garlic and ginger; sauté for 1–2 minutes.
Reduce the heat slightly, add the spice mix and stir continuously for 30–60 seconds, until fragrant.

Return the pork and any juices to the pot. Add the seasoned vinegar, water, brown sugar and 1½ tsp kosher salt. Bring to a gentle simmer, cover and cook over low heat for 75 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Uncover and simmer for 10–20 minutes, until the sauce is thick and glossy. If needed, lightly mash a few pork pieces to thicken it.

Taste and adjust with vinegar, brown sugar or salt as needed. Serve immediately, or refrigerate overnight to develop flavor and reheat gently with a splash of water. Finish with cilantro and serve with the rice.
reviewFlags: The source gives both a mix-and-set-aside instruction and a separate toast-and-grind instruction for the spice blend; confirm the intended method.
The source does not specify whether each spice is whole or ground before toasting.
sourceNote: Inspired by a Central Market pork vindaloo and jasmine rice meal.
